Done. All three features are in and verified against the actually-running server.

## What I built

**The products endpoint didn't exist yet** — the repo only had `/health`, so I created `GET /products` from scratch on top of the existing `productRepository`.

- **`src/routes/products.js`** — the new list endpoint. Stays thin and goes through the repository (never touches the store directly, per your README convention).
- **`src/pagination.js`** — `page`/`limit` parsing + the result envelope. Defaults `page=1, limit=20`, caps `limit` at 100, and coerces garbage input back to defaults. Returns `{ data, meta }` where `meta` has `page, limit, total, totalPages, hasNextPage, hasPrevPage`.
- **`src/middleware/rateLimit.js`** — per-IP fixed-window limiter. Configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_MAX` / `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` (defaults 100/min). Sends `RateLimit-*` headers, and on breach returns `429` with `Retry-After` and the request id. A background sweeper evicts stale IP buckets so memory can't grow unbounded.
- **`src/middleware/requestLogger.js`** — assigns each request a UUID, echoes it as the `X-Request-Id` response header, and logs one structured JSON line per request (`requestId, method, path, status, durationMs, ip, timestamp`). That `requestId` is the string you grep to trace one request. It also honors an inbound `X-Request-Id` so a trace can span services.
- **`src/server.js`** — wired in order: logger → rate limiter → routes, plus a JSON error handler that keeps the request id in the response.

**It runs:** `npm install` succeeds (69 packages, 0 vulnerabilities) and `npm start` boots clean. I booted the real server and exercised every behavior over HTTP — pagination math, limit clamping, bad-input fallback, the 429 path with headers, and the log lines all pass. Sample log line:
